newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to launch new two-yr zero coupon T-note.
newsitem.headline: Greece to launch new two-yr zero coupon T-note.

text.p: Greece will issue a new two-year zero coupon Treasury note on January 20 along with other issues during the month, the finance ministry said.
These include 12-month T-bills, an auction of seven-year FRNs and three-year fixed coupon bonds.
The new state debt paper aims to cover a borrowing need of 1.5 trillion drachmas in January, deputy finance minister Nickos Christodoulakis told a press conference.
He said the country's public debt improved a touch in 1996 to 35.6 trillion drachmas or 120.5 percent of GDP.
Beginning on January 2, the finance ministry will issue 12-month T-bills at 11.20 percent, six-month T-bills at 10.50 percent and three-month T-bills at 10.20 percent.

"The rate on the new T-bills was kept at 11.20 percent in order to ease the light impact on yield as a result of the new 7.5 percent tax on earned interest that goes into effect in 1997," Christodoulakis said.
State debt paper enjoyed a tax exempt status but this ends Dec 31 1996.
Christodoulakis specified that the new 7.5 percent tax will be witheld on purchases of all new T-bill issues.
But on all other debt issues like floaters, two-year T-notes and three-year coupon bonds the tax will be paid upon maturity, the deputy finance minister said.
